response.rationale: Homogeneous T2-isointense corpus callosum mass with marked CSF protein elevation and no CSF pleocytosis favors primary CNS lymphoma over glioblastoma, which is usually T2-hyperintense and heterogeneous. Negative infectious and autoimmune workup further reduces PML, toxoplasmosis, and ADEM.

rejected.why: PML typically lacks rim enhancement and mass effect; HIV negative and very high CSF protein are atypical.
ADEM usually has CSF pleocytosis and T2-hyperintense multifocal lesions, not a solitary T2-isointense enhancing mass.
No immunosuppression or HIV, negative CSF cultures, and homogeneous T2-isointense mass are not typical for toxoplasmosis.
Neuroinflammation is nonspecific and specific autoimmune/infectious markers are negative; imaging suggests a neoplastic mass.
Glioblastoma is usually T2-hyperintense and heterogeneous with irregular necrosis, whereas this lesion is homogeneous and T2-isointense, favoring lymphoma.
